headline: Anthropic mathematician claims Riemann Hypothesis proof
dek: The Verge, SiliconANGLE and Engadget report the proof has not been independently verified.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: A claim, not a fact
body: Levent Alpöge, an Anthropic mathematician, says he proved the Riemann Hypothesis with help from Claude (The Verge, SiliconANGLE, Engadget).
He posted it on his own site, and Anthropic has not commented (SiliconANGLE, The Verge).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: How the proof works
s3.body: According to Alpöge, the proof is written in Lean.

points.t: A language that tests each logical step by computer (SiliconANGLE).
The proof runs more than 250,000 pages (SiliconANGLE, Engadget).
He says it also resolves the generalized version (The Verge, SiliconANGLE).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Why the problem matters
body: It is a Millennium Prize problem with a $1 million award (The Verge, SiliconANGLE, Engadget).
It concerns how prime numbers are distributed, per The Verge.

items.t: Outside mathematicians must still check the proof (The Verge, Engadget).
Checking it may take a long time (The Verge, Engadget).
OpenAI also claims math progress, unconfirmed (The Verge).

caption.hook: An Anthropic mathematician claims a Riemann Hypothesis proof made with Claude.
body: Levent Alpöge says he proved the Riemann Hypothesis, a Millennium Prize problem, with help from Claude, according to The Verge, SiliconANGLE and Engadget. He posted it on his own site, and Anthropic has not commented. The proof reportedly runs more than 250,000 pages and is written in Lean, a language that checks each step (SiliconANGLE, Engadget).

Keep in mind: the claim has not been independently verified, and mathematicians outside Anthropic still need to review the proof (The Verge, Engadget). Until then it is an allegation, not a confirmed result.
